positive: A ready Phase 2A.2 projection result can mint one immutable sealed active-run binding that records the exact run identity, pack path, pack fingerprint, projection fingerprint, source-resolution fingerprint, project identity, trust posture, and compatibility mode.
Resolving an active run validates the binding seal, the complete bound pack inventory, its projection receipt, and every linked fingerprint without consulting current.json.
Changing current.json after binding affects future selection only and never retargets an existing valid run.

A bounded legacy schema-v1 continuation is explicitly classified as legacy-read-only and can resolve only an already-authorized legacy run; it cannot mint a new Full binding or be promoted to schema v2.
Read-only status reports package, projection, selector, frozen-run, trust, compatibility, and provisioning-needed state without changing the filesystem.
Explicit provision service behavior reuses the Phase 2A.2 offline transaction and returns created or reused projection identity without creating run authority.

Focused proof covers binding creation and reuse, selector changes after binding, complete fingerprint validation, missing or altered packs and receipts, incompatible and unsafe state, bounded legacy continuation, read-only status, explicit provision, and zero network access.
negative: Phase 2B.1 never contacts the network, executes pack content, mutates source bundle bytes, rewrites an existing active-run binding, follows symlinks, trusts current.json for an active run, or silently upgrades legacy state.
Missing, altered, stale, incompatible, conflicting, or unsafe bound state fails closed with categorical issues and leaves source, pack, selector, and run state unchanged.
A legacy schema-v1 pack can support only an already-authorized bounded continuation and never authorizes a new Full run.
